        ### Question
        A 5-day-old male is brought to your office by his mother. The infant is experiencing bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, and overall failure to thrive. A contrast enema shows a transition point at the transverse colon between dilated ascending colon and non-distended distal portion of the colon. Which of the following is the most likely etiology of this patient's disease?

        ### Options
        opa. Muscle hypertrophy
opb. Mechanical bowel obstruction
opc. CFTR gene mutation
opd. Meiotic nondisjunction
ope. Failure of neural crest cell migration

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "Bilious vomiting" -> "suggests obstruction in the gastrointestinal tract" -> "Mechanical bowel obstruction" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Abdominal distension" -> "indicates accumulation of gas or fluid" -> "often seen in bowel obstruction" -> "Mechanical bowel obstruction" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Transition point at transverse colon" -> "indicates a blockage or structural anomaly" -> "Mechanical bowel obstruction" -> 88%
CHAIN: "Failure to thrive" -> "common in conditions affecting nutrient absorption or severe systemic illness" -> "possible Mechanical bowel obstruction" -> 80%
CHAIN: "CFTR gene mutation" -> "leads to cystic fibrosis" -> "commonly causes meconium ileus in neonates" -> "unclear relation to current symptoms without further evidence of cystic fibrosis" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Failure of neural crest cell migration" -> "leads to Hirschsprung disease" -> "typically presents with a transition zone in rectosigmoid area, not transverse colon" -> "less likely given the location of transition point" -> 55%
CHAIN: "Muscle hypertrophy" -> "could theoretically cause intestinal obstruction if affecting intestinal muscles" -> "no common conditions link muscle hypertrophy to neonatal bowel obstruction" -> "unlikely cause" -> 30%
CHAIN: "Meiotic nondisjunction" -> "leads to chromosomal abnormalities like Down syndrome" -> "associated with Hirschsprung disease but not specifically with transition point at transverse colon" -> "unlikely cause" -> 40%
